subject: history
topicDisplay: The Age Of The Crusades C1071 1204
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In which year did Mussolini lead the March on Rome that brought him to power?
questions.explain: The Fascist March on Rome of October 1922 prompted King Victor Emmanuel III to appoint Mussolini Prime Minister.

questions.q: What document, proclaiming universal natural rights, did the National Assembly adopt in August 1789?
options: The Civil Constitution of the Clergy
The Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
questions.explain: The Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen was adopted on 26 August 1789, asserting liberty, equality and popular sovereignty.

questions.q: In which year did the First Crusade capture Jerusalem?
questions.explain: The crusaders stormed and captured Jerusalem on 15 July 1099, establishing Christian rule in the Holy City.

questions.q: Which Muslim leader recaptured Jerusalem from the crusaders in 1187?
questions.explain: Saladin defeated the crusaders at Hattin and retook Jerusalem in October 1187, triggering the Third Crusade.

questions.q: At which 1187 battle did Saladin annihilate the army of the Kingdom of Jerusalem?
questions.explain: At the Battle of Hattin (4 July 1187) Saladin destroyed the Frankish field army, leaving the kingdom defenceless.

questions.q: The 1929 agreement that reconciled the Fascist state with the papacy was known as the:
questions.explain: The Lateran Pacts of 1929 recognised Vatican City as an independent state and settled the long-standing 'Roman Question'.

questions.q: In which year did Napoleon crown himself Emperor of the French?
questions.explain: Napoleon crowned himself Emperor in Notre-Dame on 2 December 1804, in the presence of Pope Pius VII.

questions.q: At which 1815 battle was Napoleon finally defeated, ending his Hundred Days?
questions.explain: Napoleon was decisively defeated at Waterloo on 18 June 1815 by Wellington and Blucher, leading to his exile to St Helena.

questions.q: The murder of which socialist deputy in 1924 provoked a major crisis for Mussolini's regime?
questions.explain: The kidnapping and murder of Giacomo Matteotti in June 1924, after he denounced Fascist violence, triggered the Matteotti Crisis.

questions.q: Which English king was a leading commander of the Third Crusade?
questions.explain: Richard I ('the Lionheart') led the Third Crusade (1189-92), recapturing Acre and negotiating a truce with Saladin.

questions.q: The fall and execution of Robespierre, ending the Terror, occurred in which month and year?
questions.explain: Robespierre was overthrown in the Thermidorian Reaction and guillotined on 28 July 1794 (10 Thermidor Year II).

questions.q: In which year did Napoleon Bonaparte seize power in the coup of 18-19 Brumaire?
questions.explain: Napoleon overthrew the Directory in the coup of Brumaire (9-10 November 1799), establishing the Consulate with himself as First Consul.

questions.q: In which year did Fascist Italy invade Abyssinia (Ethiopia)?
questions.explain: Italy invaded Abyssinia in October 1935, completing its conquest in 1936 and provoking League of Nations sanctions.

questions.q: Which factor is most commonly cited as intensifying the witch craze in the period of religious conflict?
options: Confessional rivalry between Protestants and Catholics after the Reformation
questions.explain: Reformation-era confessional anxiety and rivalry between Protestants and Catholics heightened fears of diabolical conspiracy.

questions.q: Which development is most associated with the decline of witch persecutions after c1680?
options: The growth of scientific rationalism and judicial scepticism
The spread of the printing press
questions.explain: The rise of scientific rationalism and increasing scepticism among judges and elites undermined the legal basis for prosecutions.

questions.q: Which King of Scotland and England wrote the 1597 treatise Daemonologie?
questions.explain: James VI of Scotland (later James I of England) published Daemonologie in 1597, reflecting his interest in witchcraft.

questions.q: In which year was Louis XVI executed by guillotine?
questions.explain: Convicted of treason by the National Convention, Louis XVI was guillotined on 21 January 1793.

questions.q: What political entity did the crusaders establish after capturing Constantinople in 1204?
questions.explain: After the 1204 sack, the crusaders founded the Latin Empire of Constantinople, fracturing the Byzantine state.

questions.q: The 1917 Italian military catastrophe against Austro-German forces is known as the Battle of which place?
questions.explain: At Caporetto in October-November 1917 the Italian army suffered a devastating defeat, deepening post-war disillusionment.

questions.q: In which year did Italy join the First World War, declaring war on Austria-Hungary?
questions.explain: Italy entered the war on the Entente side in May 1915 after the secret Treaty of London promised territorial gains.

questions.q: Which 1486 treatise became a notorious manual for identifying and prosecuting witches?
questions.explain: The Malleus Maleficarum ('Hammer of Witches'), published in 1486, provided a framework for detecting and trying witches.

questions.q: Which Italian maritime republic played the dominant role in diverting the Fourth Crusade?
questions.explain: Venice, under Doge Enrico Dandolo, supplied the fleet and redirected the crusade first to Zara and then to Constantinople.

questions.q: The ideological and political division of Europe after 1945 between Western and Soviet spheres became known as the:
questions.explain: Churchill popularised the phrase 'Iron Curtain' in 1946 to describe the Soviet-imposed division of Europe during the Cold War.

questions.q: Which ideology, emphasising class struggle and the abolition of private property, drew on the writings of Karl Marx?
questions.explain: Communism, rooted in Marx's analysis of class conflict, sought a classless society through the abolition of private property.

questions.q: The radical phase of the Revolution known as the Terror was dominated by which committee?
questions.explain: The Committee of Public Safety, with Robespierre prominent, directed the Terror of 1793-94 through revolutionary tribunals and emergency powers.

questions.q: In which year did King Louis XVI summon the Estates-General, an act that triggered the chain of events leading to revolution in France?
questions.explain: Facing fiscal collapse, Louis XVI summoned the Estates-General, which first met at Versailles in May 1789 for the first time since 1614.

questions.q: On what date did the Parisian crowd storm the Bastille?
questions.explain: The fortress-prison of the Bastille fell to the Parisian crowd on 14 July 1789, a symbolic blow against royal despotism.

questions.q: Which five-man executive governed France from 1795 until Napoleon's coup?
questions.explain: The Directory, a five-member executive established under the Constitution of 1795, governed France until the coup of Brumaire in 1799.

questions.q: In which year did Pope Urban II preach the sermon at Clermont that launched the First Crusade?
questions.explain: Pope Urban II called for the First Crusade at the Council of Clermont in November 1095.

questions.q: What was abolished by the National Assembly's decrees of 4-11 August 1789?
questions.explain: On the night of 4 August 1789 the Assembly abolished feudal privileges and seigneurial dues, dismantling the legal framework of the ancien regime.
